item.description: arXiv:2610.17454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for $k=4$ the quantum uniformity measures are norms, whereas for every $k\geq5$ the triangle inequality fails. This gives a complete answer to an open question of Bu, Gu, and Jaffe. The $k=4$ case is proved using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the quantum uniformity pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{Q^4}$ introduced here, together with the triangle inequality in a suitable finite-dimensional Bochner $L^8$ space. For $k\geq5$, we construct systems of linear equations over a finite field and derive a contradiction from the structure theory of norming linear systems.
item.dc:creator: Berke \"Unal

item.title: The $2$-co-lacunary subsequence principle for arbitrary noncommutative $L_1$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every von Neumann algebra \(\M\), we prove that each bounded sequence in the Haagerup space \(L_1(\M)=\M_*\) admits either a norm-convergent subsequence or a \(2\)-co-lacunary subsequence. This answers an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina \cite[Remark~3.11]{ParcetRandrianantoanina2006} and removes both hyperfiniteness and semifiniteness.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang, Yunpeng Zhu

item.title: Radon Transforms of Projection Functions and Aleksandrov-Fenchel Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.18268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Radon transforms on Grassmannians define two families of geometric operators on convex bodies when applied to their projection functions. On the one hand, these are Minkowski's projection body maps and on the other hand these operators coincide on origin-symmetric bodies with the mean section body maps introduced by Goodey and Weil in 1992. Over the past two decades various sharp isoperimetric inequalities for projection bodies were shown to also hold for mean section bodies. However, an analogue of Lutwak's log-concavity inequalities for the intrinsic volumes of projection bodies remained open for mean section bodies. We establish new Aleksandrov--Fenchel inequalities for averages of certain mixed volumes and apply them to show that also all the intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies are indeed log-concave.
item.dc:creator: Leo Brauner, Oscar Ortega-Moreno, Franz E. Schuster

item.title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed). The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the identification of a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states with a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere of the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Maksim E. Shirokov, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Auerbach bases of real $\ell_p^n$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2302.00664v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Auerbach bases of the space $\ell^n_p$, and in particular, prove that $\ell_p^n$ has only finitely many Auerbach bases for $p>n$ and $1<p<n/(n-1)$. An explicit one-parameter family in $\ell_4^4$ shows that the condition $p>n$ cannot in general be weakened to $p\geq n$. Further, we provide an explicit classification of the Auerbach bases in dimension two and three.
item.dc:creator: Arun Maiti, Debmalya Sain

item.title: Beurling and Model subspaces invariant under a universal operator
item.description: arXiv:2406.07774v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the Beurling and model subspaces of the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb D)$ that are invariant under the composition operators $C_{\phi_a}$, where $\phi_a(z)=az+1-a$ and $0<a<1$. These operators have universal translates in the sense of Rota and provide a function-theoretic approach to the Hilbert space Invariant Subspace Problem. For each fixed $a$, a Beurling subspace $\Theta H^2$ is invariant precisely when \[ \Theta(z)=\lambda B(z)\exp\left(-c\,\frac{1+z}{1-z}\right), \qquad |\lambda|=1,\quad c\ge0, \] where $B$ is a possibly constant Blaschke product satisfying $m_B(w)\le m_B(\phi_a(w))$ for every $w\in\mathbb D$, with $m_B$ denoting zero multiplicity. For every affine self-map $\phi(z)=\alpha z+\beta$ with $0<|\alpha|<1$, we show that the nonzero invariant model spaces are exactly the spaces of polynomials of bounded degree. We also recover the corresponding Beurling and model subspace classifications for the classical Ces\`aro operator. Finally, we characterize when a cyclic invariant subspace contains a nonzero function analytic across $1$ through its intersections with model spaces whose boundary spectra omit $1$, and exhibit an infinite-dimensional cyclic subspace containing an eigenvector but no such analytic function.
item.dc:creator: Ben Hur Eidt, Waleed Noor

item.title: Testing compactness of linear operators
item.description: arXiv:2411.17654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(F_i)$ be a sequence of sets in a Banach space $X$. For what sequences does the condition $$ \lim_{i\to \infty} \sup_{f_i\in F_i} \|Tf_i\|_Y=0 $$ hold for every Banach space $Y$ and every compact operator $T:X\to Y$? We answer this question by giving sufficient (and necessary) criteria for such sequences. We illustrate the applicability of the criteria by examples from the literature and by characterizing the $L^p\to L^p$ compactness of dyadic paraproducts on general measure spaces through introducing a space of vanishing mean oscillations with respect to mass (as opposed to length) of cubes.
item.dc:creator: Timo S. H\"anninen, Tuomas Oikari

item.title: Connectedness properties of small minimal clusters in Riemannian or Finsler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2504.20587v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that in a compact Riemannian manifold, the $m$-minimal clusters of sufficiently small total volume are connected and with small diameter, while in a more general Finsler manifold they are done by at most $m$ connected components of small diameter. We apply these results to calculate the asymptotic expansion of the multi-isoperimetric profile at the first nontrivial order, for small volumes.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Nardulli, Aldo Pratelli

item.title: Rellich-Kondrachov type theorems on the half-space with general singular weights
item.description: arXiv:2508.01978v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Rellich-Kondrachov type theorems on the half-space $\mathbb{H}^{N+1}=\{(y, x) \in \left.\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^N: y>0\right\}$ endowed with the general weighted measure $\mu_w:=y^c \phi(|z|) d z$, where $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\phi$ is a suitable Borel measurable function. We establish a necessary and sufficient characterization for the compactness of the immersion $H_{\mu_w}^1\left(\mathbb{H}^{N+1}\right) \hookrightarrow L_{\mu_w}^2\left(\mathbb{H}^{N+1}\right)$. We prove that compactness holds if and only if the measure has finite mass and satisfies a "Global Tightness" condition, which we characterize via a coercive tail inequality (Lyapunov condition) and, in the singular case $c \leq-1$, a weighted Hardy inequality. These results generalize recent work on Gaussian weights to a broader class of radial potentials defined by abstract massvanishing conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan Zhao

item.title: Hilbert transforms on Coxeter groups and groups acting on buildings
item.description: arXiv:2508.18176v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study Hilbert transforms and their boundedness on $L_p$-spaces associated with Coxeter groups and groups acting on buildings. We establish new models for Hilbert transforms on these groups through the geometric objects they act on, and we show that these Hilbert transforms satisfy a Cotlar identity which was developed in earlier work of Mei and Ricard, and that of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and the second named author, thus conclude the $L_p$-boundedness. We manage to solve the problem firstly for the case when the Coxeter group satisfies a certain nested condition, and then extend it to any finitely generated Coxeter groups and groups that admit actions on buildings satisfying the nested condition. Our results give the first example of groups with property (F$\mathbb{R}$) on which $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms can be defined, and generalize the work of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and the second named author for groups acting on simplicial trees.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Qi Lu, Runlian Xia

item.title: Bornological LB-spaces and idempotent adjunctions
item.description: arXiv:2511.08528v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The notion of an LB-space was introduced by Grothendieck in his 1953 th\`{e}se, referring to a countable colimit of Banach spaces taken within the category of locally convex topological vector spaces, and refining prior work done by Dieudonn\'{e}, Schwartz and K\"othe. Recently, two different notions of `bornological LB-spaces' emerged: one, given by Stempfhuber, refers to countable colimits of Banach spaces as well, but now taken in the category of bornological vector spaces. The other one, given by Bambozzi, Ben-Bassat and Kremnizer, refers to bornologifications of regular LB-spaces, i.e., of LB-spaces in the Grothendieck sense having the additional property that every bounded subset of the colimit is contained and bounded in one of its Banach steps. In this note, we show that the two notions are distinct, but nevertheless closely related. This involves, in particular, an intimate study of the idempotent adjunction of the bornologification and topologification functors.
item.dc:creator: Jack Kelly, Lenny Neyt, Sven-Ake Wegner

item.title: A Stone-Weierstrass approximation theorem for monotone functions
item.description: arXiv:2512.03633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an approximation theorem for continuous non-decreasing functions on compact preordered spaces, leading to an algebraic characterization of their corresponding function spaces. As an application, we prove that the family of positive non-decreasing rational functions with non-negative coefficients can uniformly approximate all non-negative continuous non-decreasing functions on compact intervals. An explicit approximation formula of this type is provided.
item.dc:creator: Ettore Minguzzi

item.title: Connections between Essential Norm, Bhatia-\v{S}emrl Property and Strong Subdifferentiability of Operators on Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2512.15208v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Birkhoff-James orthogonality in spaces of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces through the Bhatia-\v{S}emrl property. We investigate the interplay among three key properties of bounded linear operators: strong subdifferentiability, the Bhatia-\v{S}emrl property, and the condition that the essential norm is strictly less than the operator norm. If $X$ is a Banach space with a $1$-unconditional basis and $Y$ is any Banach space, we show that every nonzero operator $T \in B(X, Y)$ satisfying the Bhatia-\v{S}emrl property satisfies $\|T\|_e<\|T\|$. We identify a class of pairs of Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ for which the inequality $\|T\|_e<\|T\|$ can be characterized in terms of strong subdifferentiability of the operator norm at $T$ and compactness of the norm attainment set of $T$. We also study norm one projections satisfying the Bhatia-\v{S}emrl property and provide examples of operators that possess this property.
item.dc:creator: C. R. Jayanarayanan, Rishit R Rajpopat

item.title: Bounded Toeplitz operators and unbounded projected multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2601.10711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a smooth, nonnegative radial symbol $g$ on $\mathbb C$ whose Toeplitz operator on Bargmann--Fock space is positive with singular values decaying faster than every exponential, while projected multiplication $f\mapsto P(gf)$ has no bounded extension from the ambient Gaussian $L^2$ space. All heat transforms of $g$ at positive times are Schwartz functions, and $g\in L^p(dA)$ for every $0<p<2$. We also construct smooth real symbols realizing every possible set of heat boundedness times. Any prescribed positive threshold may be included or excluded, with Schwartz transforms at every later time. All these symbols satisfy the coherent state domain condition, and all heat integrals converge absolutely.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: Constructive Peter--Weyl Theory: What Is Known and What Remains Open
item.description: arXiv:2603.17618v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: What is known about constructive Peter-Weyl theory, and what remains open? This expository article separates established theorems, comparisons between formulations, and questions requiring further investigation in the Bishop-Coquand-Spitters line. Its central finding is that constructive Peter-Weyl theory already has an established compact-group approximation core: under specified analytic and Gelfand hypotheses, finite-rank central convolution projections converge strongly in the Haar L2 norm. We make these hypotheses and the projection-kernel normalization explicit, and record the resulting spectral Hilbert completion. This answers the question of completion affirmatively for that precise core theorem. Broader claims about the whole classical package or its validity across constructive foundations require separate comparisons; uniform approximation, irreducible representation data, and point-set recovery are not inferred from strong convergence alone. The historical problems of left-right almost periodicity and universal Bohr compactification are examined with a dated follow-up literature review, distinguishing related progress from a verified resolution. A sufficient metric realization criterion, finite examples, and a separate nonassociative outlook clarify the scope of the established method. An extended appendix proves the classical Peter-Weyl theorem through Haar averaging, convolution, spectral density, point separation, and irreducible orthogonality. Stage-by-stage comparisons explain which arguments transfer constructively and which require additional data or a different proof. The article therefore identifies what is proved and what additional statements or data remain to be examined, without treating an unidentified resolution as proof that a problem is currently open.
item.dc:creator: Takao Inou\'{e}

item.title: Ideal structure of $\ell^p$ uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.11586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a uniformly locally finite coarse space $(X,\mathcal E)$ and $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty]$, we classify the nonzero geometric ideals of the $\ell^p$ uniform Roe algebra $B_u^p(X,\mathcal E)$ by the ideals of $\mathcal E$, equivalently by ideals in the associated family of controlled partial coverings. Hence the geometric ideal lattice is canonically independent of $p$. For $p\in[1,\infty]$, we identify $B_u^p(X,\mathcal E)$ isometrically with the reduced $L^p$ operator algebra of the coarse groupoid and show that this identification preserves essential support, carrying geometric and ghostly ideals to dynamical and restrictive ideals. Under property A, controlled $p$-kernels yield a multiplier approximate identity with controlled propagation; consequently every ideal is geometric and every ghost is trivial. Thus the full ideal lattices are canonically independent of $p$ under property A. For $p\in\{0,1,\infty\}$, the complete ideal classification holds without property A; on the groupoid side, the corresponding unconditional conclusion holds for $p\in\{1,\infty\}$.
item.dc:creator: Yeong Chyuan Chung, Xinhui Du

item.title: Pettis integrability of functions with values in separable symmetrically-normed ideals and related norm estimates
item.description: arXiv:2607.02790v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we will investigate Pettis integrability of $\mathcal{C}^{\circ}_{\Phi}(\mathcal{H})$-valued functions. We will study weakly$^*$ integrable $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$-valued functions and establish sufficient conditions for such functions to be Pettis integrable as $\mathcal{C}^{\circ}_{\Phi}(\mathcal{H})$-valued functions. In addition, we prove the inequality $$\left\|\int_E\mathscr{A}^*\mathscr{B}d\mu \right\|_{\Phi^{(p)}} \leqslant \|\mathscr{A}\|_{L^q_s}\cdot\left\|\sqrt[p]{\int_E|\mathscr{B}|^pd\mu}\right\|_{\Phi^{(p)}},$$ where $\Phi^{(p)}$ is $p$-modification of the function $\Phi$ and the functions $\mathscr{A}$ and $\mathscr{B}$ belong to the suitable spaces of operator-valued functions. Finally, under some additional integrability assumptions on $\mathscr{B}$ we provide similar estimates of the Pettis norm.
item.dc:creator: Mihailo Krsti\'c, Matija Milovi\'c, Stefan Milo\v{s}evi\'c

item.title: On the Spectral Synthesis of Lipschitz Vectorizations of Persistence Diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2607.16957v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Persistence diagrams are fundamental descriptors in topological data analysis. Many statistical and machine learning methods require persistence diagrams to be mapped into vector spaces or compared through kernels. Although many persistence diagram vectorizations and persistence kernels have been proposed, there is no general framework for determining which persistence diagram vectorizations are synthesizable. Spectral synthesis asks whether the exponential monomials contained in the translation-invariant variety generated by a function span a dense subspace of that variety. We introduce uniformly discrete spectral synthesis for persistence diagram vectorizations using Fourier analysis on groups of virtual persistence diagrams. When the space of persistence intervals is separable, we prove sufficient conditions for uniformly discrete spectral synthesis and derive approximation results for virtual persistence diagrams with bounded total multiplicity. We then classify many persistence diagram vectorizations and persistence kernels from the literature by uniformly discrete spectral synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Charles Fanning, Mehmet Emin Aktas

item.title: Metric gradient flows and variational principles
item.description: arXiv:2608.01262v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that Ekeland-type variational principles can be derived from steepest descent curves in metric spaces. From this, we relate the existence of the Calabi flow to the validity of the Ekeland variational principle for the $K$-energy on the space of K\"ahler potentials.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella

item.title: The Endpoint Fractional Riesz Estimate on the Hamming Cube
item.description: arXiv:2609.03993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $1<p<2$ and $D_j$ be the discrete partial derivative on the Hamming cube $\Omega_n = \{ -1, 1\}^n$. Let $\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^nD_j$ be the discrete Laplacian. We prove the endpoint inequality \[ \left\|\left(\sum_{j=1}^n|D_jf|^2\right)^{1/2}\right\|_{p} \lesssim_p\|\Delta^{1/p}f\|_{p}, \quad \forall f:\Omega_n \to \mathbb C. \] This result answers the conjecture proposed by Naor, Eskenazis and Ivanisvili (see [BenEfraimLustPiquard, IvanisviliVolberg] or [Remark 45, EskenazisIvanisvili]). The proof relies heavily on the noncommutative semigroup BMO theory [JungeMei].
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Xu, Hao Zhang

item.title: Area operators on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series II: counterexamples and compactness criteria
item.description: arXiv:2609.06033v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study area operators $\mathbb{A}_{\mu,l}$, $0<l<\infty$, induced by positive Borel measures on the right half-plane and acting on the Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series $\mathscr H^p$, $0<p<\infty$. We first disprove a conjecture proposed by the present authors in an earlier work by constructing a probability measure, valid for all $0<p,l<\infty$, for which the associated area operator is bounded although the measure fails the proposed Carleson conditions. We then characterize the boundedness and compactness of $\mathbb{A}_{\mu,l}$ on both $\mathscr H^p$ and the Hardy space $\mathscr H^p_0$ of Dirichlet series vanishing at $+\infty$, for every $0<p,l<\infty$, via integrability conditions for the associated cone integrals. In particular, the boundedness and compactness are equivalent for these operators. We also give direct proofs of compactness under vanishing Carleson measure and compact $H_{\mathrm i}^p$-Carleson embedding hypotheses. As an application, we establish an estimate for the essential norms of bounded Volterra operators. This leads to a complete characterization of compactness for Volterra operators on $\mathscr{H}^p$ and provides a different proof of compactness for those with Dirichlet series symbols in $\operatorname{VMOA}(\mathbb C_0)$.
item.dc:creator: Jiale Chen, Maofa Wang, Zixing Yuan

item.title: Reflectionless measures with singular continuous components on Widom sets
item.description: arXiv:2609.27133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a detailed implementation of the mass-splitting construction of Nazarov, Volberg and Yuditskii for reflectionless measures with singular continuous components. The finite approximants are allowed to have isolated atoms. An exact local operation replaces each active atom by a short permanent interval and two child atoms, thereby eliminating the dependence of a future splitting scale on an already prescribed band width. Summable estimates for completed generations and fixed cylinders retain positive mass on a null Cantor set and exclude atoms in the limit. Uniform analytic estimates near the permanent intervals establish reflectionlessness and exclude endpoint singularities. A separate Green function estimate for thin pairs of intervals gives the Widom condition and regularity of the limiting compact set. The resulting probability measure has both a nonzero absolutely continuous component and a nonzero singular continuous component.
item.dc:creator: Long Li

item.title: Inverse-Limit Detection Envelopes as Calkin Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.32330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a unital Banach algebra $A$ with $\|1_A\|=1$ and a decreasing sequence $(I_r)$ of proper closed two-sided ideals of finite codimension, we introduce the bounded detection envelope $$\widehat A:=\operatorname{Env}^{b}_{(I_r)}(A)=\varprojlim^{b}(A/I_r,\pi_r^s),\qquad \|(a_r)_r\|=\sup_r\|a_r\|.$$ Combining vector-valued Bourgain--Delbaen extensions, oracle Turing-machine recursion, and Argyros--Haydon operator analysis, we construct a separable Banach space $X$ such that, isometrically as unital Banach algebras, $$\operatorname{Cal}(X)=\mathcal{B}(X)/\mathcal{K}(X)\simeq\widehat A. $$ We also characterize these envelopes as the unital Banach algebras with norm-one units admitting an isometric predual and countably many jointly faithful weak-star-to-norm continuous finite-dimensional unital representations. Applications include arbitrary finite-dimensional unital Banach algebras with norm-one units and their countable $\ell_\infty$-sums, as well as unitized coordinatewise algebras over normalized $1$-unconditional boundedly complete Schauder bases. These include incidence algebras, $\ell_\infty$, and the unitization of Tsirelson's original space. Further applications concern analytic operator algebras, Fourier--Stieltjes and Fourier multiplier algebras of countable discrete groups, and classical and quantum convolution algebras. In particular, we realize $H^\infty(\mathbb D)$, $\operatorname{Mult}(H_2^2)$, $\mathcal L_2$, $M_{\mathrm{cb}}A(\mathbb F_2)$, and $C^u(O_3^+)^*$ as Calkin algebras, with their canonical norms and products.
item.dc:creator: Rui Liu, Jie Shen

item.title: Duals of separable Banach Spaces as Calkin Algebras and Universal Ideal Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2609.32334v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every separable Banach space $V$, we use an oracle-relative two-sorted finite-extension construction, whose oracle records the local rational structure of $V$, to construct a separable Banach space $X_V$ such that $$ \operatorname{Cal}(X_V)=\mathcal{B}(X_V)/\mathcal{K}(X_V)\simeq \begin{pmatrix} \mathbb{K}&0\\ V^*&\mathbb{K} \end{pmatrix} $$ as Banach algebras. The identification of $V^*$ with the Jacobson radical is isometric. Consequently, every nonzero dual Banach space with a separable predual admits, after an equivalent renorming, a unital Banach-algebra structure isomorphic to the Calkin algebra of a separable Banach space. Moreover, there is a separable Banach space $X$ such that every separable Banach space is isometric to $\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{K}(X)$ for a closed two-sided ideal $\mathcal{J}$ of $\mathcal{B}(X)$, and the subspace--ideal correspondence preserves the canonical order.
item.dc:creator: Rui Liu, Jie Shen

item.title: Stability of isometries of quantum states
item.description: arXiv:2609.37133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove dimension-independent Hyers--Ulam stability for surjective approximate isometries of the positive trace-class cone in both the trace and Bures metrics. Here $\varepsilon\geq0$ is a uniform upper bound on the additive error in preserving distances. Such an approximate isometry is uniformly approximated by a Wigner symmetry (a unitary or antiunitary conjugation), with error at most $9\varepsilon/2$ in the trace metric and $2\sqrt2\varepsilon$ in the Bures metric, even if it does not fix zero. For maps fixing zero, the trace bound improves to $3\varepsilon$ even under the hypothesis of $\delta$-surjectivity, independently of $\delta$. In infinite dimensions, we construct spectrum-preserving homeomorphisms of the full state space, including mixed states, whose distortions tend to zero in both metrics but which stay a fixed uniform distance from every Wigner symmetry. For state spaces, stability holds in each fixed finite dimension with a dimension-dependent modulus tending to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$, but no such modulus can be chosen independently of dimension.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: A New insight into the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak approach to Sobolev maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.04384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $p \in (1,\infty)$, let $\operatorname{X}=(\operatorname{X},\rho,\mu)$ be a metric measure space such that the measure $\mu$ is uniformly locally doubling and $\operatorname{X}$ supports a weak local $(1,p)$-Poincar\'e inequality. Let $(\operatorname{Y},\operatorname{d},\underline{y})$ be a complete pointed metric space. We prove that the equivalence class of a Borel map $ u:\operatorname{X} \to \operatorname{Y}$ (modulo coincidence $\mu$-a.e.) belongs to the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak--Sobolev class $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{Y})$ if and only if $h \circ u$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X})$ for every $1$-Lipschitz function $h:\operatorname{Y} \to \mathbb{R}$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Tyulenev

item.title: Domains of Monomial Convergence in Banach Sequence Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.08873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A classical phenomenon distinguishing infinite-dimensional holomorphy from its finite-dimensional counterpart is that monomial expansions of holomorphic functions need not converge absolutely. In this paper, we systematically investigate monomial convergence on complex Banach sequence spaces. We establish general structural results and give a negative answer to Lempert's problem. We then determine the domains of absolute monomial convergence for holomorphic functions on the classical Banach sequence spaces and obtain a complete classification for continuous homogeneous polynomials. As a further application, we establish a sharp comparison between two notions of convergence radius for homogeneous Taylor expansions on $\ell^1$. The methods developed here are of independent interest and may be applied in other places.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzhe Wang

item.title: An Improved Inequality between the von Neumann-Jordan and James Constants
item.description: arXiv:2610.13360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a strengthened answer to the questions posed by Alonso, Mart\'in, and Papini [Studia Math. 188 (2008), 135--150] concerning the comparison between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants . The classical inequality $\CNJ(X)\leq J(X)$ between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants was established by Takahashi and Kato [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 359 (2009), 602--609], Wang [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 138 (2010), 695--701], and Yang and Li [Appl. Math. Lett. 23 (2010), 277--281], while related sharp estimates were obtained by Kato and Takahashi [Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) Suppl. 82 (2010), 75--91]. We sharpen this inequality to $\CNJ(X)\leq\JB(X)$, where $\JB(X)$ is the Birkhoff--James orthogonal James constant introduced by Baronti and Papini [Constr. Math. Anal. 5 (2022), 37--45]. Our proof employs optimal distance ellipses and alternating contact directions.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu

item.title: Free probability via entropic optimal transport
item.description:
arXiv:2309.12196v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be compactly supported probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu  oxplus 
u$ denote their additive free convolution. We show that for all sufficiently large real $z$,  egin{equation} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \log(z - x) \, (\mu  oxplus 
u)(\mathrm{d}x) = \sup_{\Pi} \left\{ \mathbf{E}_\Pi[\log(z - (X+Y))] - H(\Pi \mid \mu \otimes 
u) ight\}, \end{equation} where the supremum is taken over all couplings $\Pi$ of $\mu$ and $
u$. Analogous formulas hold for multiplicative free convolution $\mu  oxtimes 
u$ and free compression $[\mu]_	au$. In this way, integrals of a log-potential against free convolutions can be expressed as entropic optimal transport problems. The corresponding optimal couplings admit explicit formulas, from which the standard $R$- and $S$-transform descriptions of additive and multiplicative free convolution are recovered. In particular, the optimizer $\Pi_z$ encodes the subordination equations via couplings of random variables. Our approach is based on a large deviation principle on the symmetric group, combined with the quadrature method of Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava.
item.dc:creator: Octavio Arizmendi, Samuel G. G. Johnston

item.title: Input-to-state stability in integral norms for linear infinite-dimensional systems
item.description: arXiv:2501.07680v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study integral-to-integral input-to-state stability for infinite-dimensional linear systems with inputs and trajectories in $L^p$-spaces. We start by developing the corresponding admissibility theory for linear systems with unbounded input operators. While input-to-state stability is typically characterised by exponential stability and finite-time admissibility, we show that this equivalence does not extend directly to integral norms. For analytic semigroups, we establish a precise characterisation using maximal regularity theory. Additionally, we provide direct Lyapunov theorems and construct Lyapunov functions for $L^p$-$L^q$-ISS and demonstrate the results with examples, including diagonal systems and diffusion equations.
item.dc:creator: Sahiba Arora, Andrii Mironchenko

item.title: Extendable Shift Maps and the Canonical Map on Generalized Countable Markov Shifts
item.description: arXiv:2506.07487v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain an operator-algebraic characterization of when the shift map can be continuously extended from a standard countable Markov shift $\Sigma_A$ to its generalized countable Markov shift $X_A$, a compactification of $\Sigma_A$. We show that a canonical unital completely positive map on the Exel--Laca algebra $O_A$ can be defined exactly when the shift extends continuously from $\Sigma_A$ to $X_A$, and that in this case its restriction to the maximal commutative C$^*$-subalgebra $D_A$ is a $*$-endomorphism to which the extended shift is dual. We also give a criterion on the matrix $A$ itself, in terms of the convergence of its columns, and exhibit classes of transition matrices satisfying these equivalent conditions. Column-finiteness of $A$ is necessary for the existence of the continuous extension. Finally, we construct an example in which the set of empty words is a Cantor set and the extended dynamics on it is the inverse of the dyadic odometer.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Bissacot, Iv\'an Diaz-Granados, Thiago Raszeja

item.title: Nonlinear Lebesgue spaces: Curves and geometry
item.description: arXiv:2603.09459v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is the second in a series by the author and collaborators devoted to the study of geometric and analytic properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces, that is, L^p spaces of mappings taking values in arbitrary metric spaces. The present article formalizes the pointwise description of their geometric properties---their length structure, bounds on their Alexandrov curvature as well as the definition of a velocity for absolutely continuous curves despite the lack of differential structure. To obtain this pointwise description, we first prove a nonlinear analogue of the Fubini--Lebesgue theorem, which yields an identification of L^p curves in nonlinear Lebesgue spaces with mappings taking values in the space of L^p curves. This identification of L^p curves then enables a similar identification for absolutely continuous curves, from which the pointwise description of the geometric properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces follows.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume S\'erieys (MAP5 - UMR 8145)

item.title: Stancu-Type Generalizations of Neural Network Operators with Perturbed Sampling Nodes
item.description: arXiv:2603.15671v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a Stancu-type generalization of multivariate neural network operators (NNOs) by incorporating two parameters that perturb the sampling nodes. The proposed operators extend the existing NNOs by allowing flexibility in the placement of sampling nodes. We establish the well-definedness and boundedness of the operators and prove uniform convergence on compact domains. Furthermore, quantitative error estimates are derived in terms of the modulus of continuity, leading to a convergence rate result. A perturbation theorem is also established, showing how the Stancu-type operators differ from the existing NNOs. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the influence of the Stancu parameters on the approximations and to validate the theoretical results. Finally, an application to ECG signal reconstruction is considered, demonstrating that the proposed operators effectively preserve the essential characteristics of the signal while providing accurate approximations.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Saini

item.title: Algebraic Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem for quantum measurement
item.description: arXiv:2606.09584v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an operational framework connecting the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold (KA) representation theorem to quantum information theory. By introducing and proving an algebraic, bounded-degree polynomial version of the theorem, we demonstrate that any target physical property of an unentangled multi-qubit product state can be exactly decomposed using a finite, fixed set of local ``inner'' observables and a shallow architecture of univariate polynomials. We further analyse the stability of this Quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold (QKA) representation under adversarial perturbations. In stark contrast to the pathological instabilities and severe reparameterisation sensitivities inherent to the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem, our algebraic quantum framework exhibits remarkable resilience. We prove that the representation remains stable against bounded physical perturbations acting on the inner measurement operators, and show via the Heisenberg picture that it is inherently immune to adversarial quantum channel attacks acting on the input states.
item.dc:creator: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

item.title: Tur\'an problem on the union of three intervals of equal length
item.description: arXiv:2608.15643v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper addresses the Tur\'an extremal problem on the symmetric three-interval set $\Omega_\lambda = (-1,1) \cup (\lambda-1,\lambda+1) \cup (-\lambda-1,-\lambda+1)$, $\lambda \geq 0$. We establish a discrete approximation principle relating the continuous Tur\'an problem on $\Omega_\lambda$ to the discrete Tur\'an problem on an associated finite discrete set. This enables the continuous problem to be exactly expressed as a limit of finite nonnegative trigonometric polynomial problems, which are equivalent to finite semidefinite programs. Using this framework, we compute the Tur\'an constant for integer and rational parameters $\lambda$. We further analyze the dependence of the Tur\'an constant on $\lambda$ and derive upper bounds for all $\lambda > 5$.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Ye Fu, Yue-Kun Li, Wei-Jie Wang, Xuan Wang

item.title: Riccati Stability Without Auxiliary Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2609.06275v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the 2004 collection \emph{Unsolved Problems in Mathematical Systems and Control Theory}, Erik Verriest posed the problem of characterizing Riccati stability ``without invoking additional matrices.'' We give such a characterization through a scalar invariant of the resolvent family. The invariant is defined by covariance balances using at most $n^2+1$ frequency--direction pairs. A finite-dimensional separation argument shows that this covariance radius equals the optimal common ellipsoidal norm of the resolvent family. Combined with the strict bounded real lemma, this yields a necessary and sufficient condition for Riccati stability involving only the Hurwitz property of the first matrix and a single scalar inequality. The invariant reduces to the ordinary spectral radius for one matrix, lies between the pointwise spectral-radius and unscaled small-gain levels of the resolvent family, and coincides with the operator-space spectral radius of Shalit and Shamovich for the natural resolvent function space. The main results have been formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Humpherys

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce several notions of resonance for systems exhibiting weak or partial dissipation: $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, with $A$ the generator of a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. We refer to resonance as the phenomenon where a time-periodic $f$ may yield an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, unbounded growth may depend on topological choices, and several ``resonances" may occur. Classically, existence of $T$-periodic $u$ under $T$-periodic $f$ is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. Consequently, its failure permits unbounded solution growth and we elucidate that connection through properties of $S(t)$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and provide an associated resonance taxonomy. The growth rate of ~$||(A-\lambda I)^{-1}||_H$ on ~$i\R$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$, and, for rapid growth in $\lambda$, that gap can be infinite. In this case, we demonstrate implications for periodic solvability, and a mechanism for constructing smooth resonant forces. The theory developed here is motivated by (and demonstrated for) a hyperbolic-parabolic system, where the latter component provides the only system dissipation. Such dynamics are a simplification of fluid-structure phenomena, which demonstrate strong stability but do not provide unconditional periodic well-posedness. Though point-spectral resonance is ruled out, we note that $\mathcal R(I-S(T))\neq H$. Our main result here shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, a classical heat-wave system possesses periods $T$ which yield infinite derivative loss and, via supporting results, yield resonance with smooth forcing.
item.dc:creator: Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster

item.title: $W^*$-categories are von Neumann
item.description: arXiv:2609.30015v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A $C^*$-category is to a $C^*$-algebra what a groupoid is to a group. An example is the category of Hilbert spaces and bounded linear maps, and indeed, every $C^*$-category can be represented as a sub-$*$-category of this. Analogously, a $W^*$-category is a $C^*$-category where every object has a predual, and we might expect a representation theory on Hilbert spaces where the resulting morphism spaces are $\sigma$-weakly closed. We identify a gap in the literature here, stemming from the (perhaps surprising) fact that a $C^*$-algebra can have a non-isometric predual and yet not be a $W^*$-algebra. Using the theory of dual TROs (ternary rings of operators) we repair this gap, and along the way, also give further justification to arguments in the literature about dual TROs. Motivated by the theory of Dual Banach Algebras, we offer an alternative axiomatisation of $W^*$-categories where we allow non-isometric preduals of the hom spaces, but require that they are additionally bimodules in a certain sense. This involves the theory of self-dual Hilbert $C^*$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Daws

item.title: Discontinuous Generalized Hyperbolicity and Structural Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.04179v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study diffeomorphisms of Banach spaces satisfying generalized hyperbolicity: the stable and unstable subspaces are invariant only up to inclusion, need not depend continuously on the point, and expansivity may fail. On closed manifolds, this condition is equivalent to Axiom~A with strong transversality. We introduce a continuous-selection method that converts uniform orbitwise estimates into bounded continuous solutions of cohomological equations for generalized-hyperbolic cocycles. For diffeomorphisms in the uniform global \(C^1\) category, this yields continuous semiconjugacies in both directions under sufficiently small bounded Lipschitz perturbations, and topological stability in the sense of Walters. For the infinite product of one-dimensional Morse-Smale systems on \(\ell^p(\mathbb Z)\), \(1\leq p\leq\infty\), we construct compatible forward and reverse cohomological solution operators and prove structural stability, including for perturbations that couple coordinates, although the product is not expansive. For \(p=\infty\) this gives a structurally stable diffeomorphism with uncountably many hyperbolic fixed points, in contrast with the finitely many basic sets of Axiom~A diffeomorphisms. The cocycle analysis yields Lipschitz shadowing for the induced operator on bounded continuous vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Tikhomirov

item.title: A constrained log-HLS inequality and its associated Wasserstein flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.05356v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a log-Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev (log-HLS) inequality under constraints and a naturally induced Wasserstein flow. The constrained log-HLS inequality is dual, in a variational sense, to the constrained Trudinger-Moser-Onofri-Aubin inequality. The corresponding gradient-flow formulation leads to a parabolic-elliptic Patlak-Keller-Segel (PKS) system whose global dynamics exhibit a dichotomy between global existence and finite-time blow-up depending on the initial mass. Remarkably, the constraint raises the critical mass threshold of the flow by a factor of two compared with the unconstrained setting. This provides a distinct mechanism for suppressing blow-up from those arising in related formulations of the PKS-system, where blow-up is mitigated through additional effects such as a forcing term, coupling with a fluid equation, or the ambient flow generated by harmonic perturbations of the Newtonian potential.
item.dc:creator: Monideep Ghosh, Debabrata Karmakar, Reetaj Sinha, Kartikey Verma

item.title: Fractional gradients and nonlocal PDEs in variable exponent spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.08253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a theory of distributional Riesz fractional gradients in variable exponent Lebesgue spaces and introduce the associated nonlocal Sobolev spaces. Moreover, Sobolev, Hardy, Morrey, and Trudinger-type inequalities are established, and a fractional fundamental theorem of calculus is derived. As an application, we study nonlinear variational problems with nonstandard growth and establish existence and Euler--Lagrange equations for minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Susana Moura, Cornelia Schneider
